newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss move toward dropping air traffic monopoly.
newsitem.headline: Swiss move toward dropping air traffic monopoly.

text.p: The Swiss cabinet said on Wednesday that it approved a Transport Ministry proposal to amend existing laws and remove Swissair's monopoly in Switzerland as another step toward liberalising the Swiss market.

The current monopoly situation is no longer appropriate in a liberal environment, especially in view of Swiss wishes to take part in a European Union's market, the Swiss transport ministry said in a statement.
The new rules, if passed into law, would allow other Swiss-based air carriers to compete for routes which until now have automatically gone to Swissair.
The law change would not affect existing route agreements, a Swissair spokesman said.
SAirGroup, parent of Swissair, said in a statement that it supported the move, noting that existing rights of the airline would be protected.
